summary: The earlier MAJOR is fixed. In ComparisonRange.messages, awaiting starts true and is set true by every in-range outgoing row, so a follow-up resets the answer wait. The first incoming row after it is held up to max(quiet, 86400) s, then awaiting goes false and the 1800 s rule applies. Both comparisons are strict '>', so exactly 1800 s and exactly one day still belong. The 7-day direct window uses '<=' and its boundary tests are correct. An unanswered prompt releases at 24 h. An own-send takes the chat back and re-arms the answer wait. Deferring direct-thread insertion while busy, webBroadcastBusy or a web session is sending is sound: lastDataVersion is only recorded after a successful insert, so the next poll retries, and directThread already refuses while any member is .sending. The new test asserts the intended behaviour: 31 min first answer held, 23 h held, 1801 s gap released, 48 h unanswered releases, and a follow-up-reset case that would fail under the old 30 min rule. I found no routing, duplicate-thread, draft-loss or focus-taking regressions. Reviewed by reading only; no Swift toolchain here.

findings.detail: While a web broadcast or web send is in flight (webBroadcastBusy or isSending), refreshIfChanged does not guard on them, so every poll re-runs the full refresh (per-chat DB reads and reconcile) because lastDataVersion is held back. Harmless and self-healing, but a long web send means repeated work. Consider recording the version and retrying the insert from the send-completion path instead.

A contact's unrelated message arriving within 24 h of an unanswered prompt, or within 24 h of an unanswered own follow-up, stays in that conversation instead of the direct thread. This is the intended trade-off of answerPeriod, but it is worth a line in docs/architecture.md, since the wait now covers every own follow-up, not only the first prompt.

max(quiet, answerPeriod) means a caller passing quiet above one day silently uses quiet for the answer wait too. That is fine for the current callers, which use the default. The doc comment on messages(...) is one very long line (~170 chars).

The demo late-message helper discards the Bool from startDirectThreads. If the demo is busy at that moment, the thread insert is skipped and demo mode never retries, because refresh returns early in demo. It affects the preview flag only.
